sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: u_1(x,z) \leq y \leq u_2(x,z) \big\}.]

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

If [MATH: R] is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of [MATH: f(x,y,z)] over [MATH: R] as a mixed integral, as follows:

[MATH: \iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[\int_{u_1(x,z)}^{u_2(x,z)} f(x,y,z)\,\textrm d y \right] \,\textrm d A]

In our case, we have

[MATH: u_1(x,z) = 0, \qquad u_2(x,z) = z+xz.]

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

[MATH: \displaystyle \iiint \limits_{S} f(x,y,z) \: \textrm{d}V = \iint\limits_{D} \left[ \int_{0}^{z+xz} f(x,y,z) \: \mathrm{d}y \right] \mathrm{d}A.]

Now, the region [MATH: D] is given by

[MATH: D =\left\{ (x,z) \: : \: -3 \leq x \leq 3, \: x \leq z \leq 2x+2 \right\}.]

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over [MATH: D] as a repeated integral, we get

[MATH: ∬_(D)[∫_{0}^{z + xz}f(x, y, z)dy]dA|= ∫_{− 3}^{3}∫_{x}^{2x + 2}[∫_{0}^{z + xz}f(x, y, z)dy]dzdx; = ∫_{− 3}^{3}∫_{x}^{2x + 2}∫_{0}^{z + xz}f(x, y, z)dydzdx.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:

Content:
[MATH: \displaystyle \iiint\limits_R 2xz \: \mathrm{d}V]

[IMG: /graphics/4ca6d9201c908c99395dc89d3e07c42b]

Content:
The region [MATH: R] is a type III region. So, our first task is to describe this region fully.

Content:
We start by drawing an arrow parallel to the [MATH: y]-axis that

Content:
- enters the region through the left surface [MATH: y=0,] and
- leave the region through the right surface [MATH: y=6-x-z,]

Content:
as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9847e021198f35d3cc5029f4b01f5c12]

Content:
So, our solid can be written as the type III region

Content:
[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 6-x-z \big\},]

Content:
where

Content:
[MATH: D = \big\{ (x,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1 \big\}]

Content:
is the projection of [MATH: R] onto the [MATH: xz]-plane, shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9f54350de21e7008572d570755ea0a0b]

Content:

Content:
[MATH: \iiint\limits_R 2xz \:\textrm{d}V
=
\iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A]

Content:
Now, since the region [MATH: D] is a type I plane region, we can express the region [MATH: R] as

Content:
[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 6-x-z \big\},]

Content:
and therefore, our mixed integral can be written as the following repeating integral:

Content:
[MATH: \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_0^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y \right] \textrm{d}A
=
\int_{0}^{3} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x]

Content:

Content:
[MATH: \int_{0}^{3} \int_{0}^{1} \int_{0}^{6-x-z} 2xz \:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x = 15.]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that

Content:

A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

[MATH: R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: (x,z) \in D, \: u_1(x,z) \leq y \leq u_2(x,z) \big\}.]

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

If [MATH: R] is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of [MATH: f(x,y,z)] over [MATH: R] as a mixed integral, as follows:
